Either God himselfe taught Adam, and he his children, or els they knew by instinct of nature, that Sacrifice must be offered to God, to acknowledge thereby his supreme dominion over man, and mans due subiection to his diuine Maiestic. And that not only in internal affection, which (as S. Augustin, and all Catholike Doctours teach) is principally required, but also by Gods goodnes, the use of corporal things. As here we see example in the law of grace and new Testament, to wit, the same which Christ instituted, and left in his Church, to continue to the end of the world. Moreover this homage or offering Sacrifice is so peculiar to God only, that albeit manie other exterior our rites and services are used both to God & men, as to be bare-head, to bow, to kneel, & the like before them, either of greas humilitie (faith S. Augustin) or of periferous flatterie, so such as are homines ciendi, venerandi, siantem eis mulium addituri, or adorandi: men to be worshipped, reverenced, and if much be given them, adored; (for this terme of adoring is also applied to men in holic Scriptures, Gen. 23. v.7.17. v.29) yet Sacrifice is due to God only, and to no creature how excellent so ever. In so much (faith the same Doctor) that as all nations found it necessary to offer Sacrifice, so none durst sacrifice unto anic, nisi ei quem Deum aut simus, aut pueramit, aut finxit; but to him whom they either knew, or thought, or fained to be God.
